back: A push or a pull, measured in newtons (N) with a force meter.
Contact: friction, air resistance, support, tension, thrust. Non-contact: gravity, magnetic, electrostatic.
Mass is the amount of matter (kg) and is the same everywhere. Weight is the pull of gravity (N) and changes with g.
$W = mg$. On Earth $g = 10$ N/kg, so a 50 kg person weighs 500 N.
The overall force when all forces are combined. Add forces in the same direction; subtract opposite ones.
Balanced: net force zero, so the motion doesn't change. Unbalanced: the object speeds up, slows down or changes direction.
An object stays at rest or keeps moving at a constant velocity unless an unbalanced force acts on it.
An object's resistance to changes in its motion. More mass means more inertia.
If A pushes on B, then B pushes on A with an equal and opposite force. The pair acts on different objects.
A diagram of one object with labelled arrows for every force on it. Arrow length shows size, and direction shows direction.

front: What does friction do, and how can you reduce it?
back: It opposes motion between surfaces. Reduce it with lubricants (oil), smoother surfaces, or wheels and ball bearings.

front: How does air resistance change with speed?
back: It increases as the speed increases. Streamlined shapes reduce it.
The constant speed of a falling object when air resistance equals its weight (balanced forces).

front: Are a book's weight and the table's support force a third-law pair?
back: No. They act on the same object (the book) and are different types of force. They are balanced forces.
